content: 1. In the study, the presence of resistant virus to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) or emtricitabine (FTC) was not detected among individuals who became infected after enrollment. However, among three participants who were retrospectively found to have been infected at the time of enrollment, one participant in the TDF/FTC group exhibited a resistant virus, and another in the placebo group showed transient low-level resistance. 2. Among women in the study, the pregnancy rate was high, at 10.3 per 100 person-years, and there were no significant differences in pregnancy rates between the study groups. 3. The Botswana TDF2 trial was a phase 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study that evaluated the safety and efficacy of daily oral TDF/FTC in 1,219 heterosexual men and women. Monthly follow-up visits were conducted, and the study drug was discontinued in women who became pregnant during the trial. 4. The efficacy of TDF/FTC in preventing HIV infection among participants of both sexes combined was 62% (95% CI: 22%-83%). Efficacy estimates did not differ significantly by sex, but the small number of endpoints limited the statistical power to detect differences. 5. Compliance with study visits was low, with 33.1% of participants failing to complete the study per protocol. However, many were re-engaged for an exit visit, and 89.3% of enrolled participants underwent a final HIV test. 6. Among participants who seroconverted after enrollment, no resistant virus was detected. 7. Nausea, vomiting, and dizziness were more commonly reported among participants assigned to TDF/FTC, particularly during the first month of use, compared to those in the placebo group. However, there were no significant differences in rates of serious clinical or laboratory adverse events between the groups. 8. The FEM-PrEP trial, a phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, evaluated the efficacy and safety of daily TDF/FTC for HIV prevention among heterosexual women in South Africa, Kenya, and Tanzania. The trial was stopped in 2011 after interim analysis indicated it was unlikely to detect a statistically significant difference in efficacy between the study groups. 9. Adherence in the FEM-PrEP trial was low, with study drug detected in plasma samples of fewer than 50% of women assigned to TDF/FTC. Nausea, vomiting (primarily in the first month), and transient, modest elevations in liver function test values were more common in the TDF/FTC group than in the placebo group. No changes in renal function were observed in either group. 10. Initial efficacy analyses in the FEM-PrEP trial showed 4.7 infections per 100 person-years in the TDF/FTC group and 5.0 infections per 100 person-years in the placebo group, with a hazard ratio of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.59-1.52), indicating no reduction in HIV incidence associated with TDF/FTC use. 11. Of the 68 women who acquired HIV during the FEM-PrEP trial, TDFor FTC-resistant virus was detected in five women: one in the placebo group and four in the TDF/FTC group. Multivariate analyses found no association between pregnancy rate and study group. 12. A phase 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of oral TDF was conducted among heterosexual women in Ghana, Cameroon, and Nigeria to assess the safety of TDF use and its efficacy in reducing HIV infection rates. The Cameroon and Nigeria sites were closed prematurely due to operational challenges, resulting in insufficient follow-up data for planned efficacy analysis. 13. Safety data from the Ghana and Cameroon sites showed no statistically significant differences in grade 3 or 4 hepatic or renal events or in reports of clinical adverse events between the TDF and placebo groups. 14. Eight HIV seroconversions occurred in the West African trial: two among women in the TDF group (rate: 0.86 per 100 person-years) and six among women in the placebo group (rate: 2.48 per 100 person-years), yielding a rate ratio of 0.35 (95% CI: 0.03-1.93; p = 0.24). No drug-resistance mutations were detected in the one participant with available blood specimens who seroconverted while taking TDF. 15. The VOICE trial (MTN-003) was a phase 2B randomized, double-blind study comparing oral (TDF or TDF/FTC) and topical vaginal (tenofovir) antiretroviral regimens against corresponding oral and topical placebos among 5,029 heterosexual women in eastern and southern Africa. In 2011, the oral TDF and topical tenofovir groups were stopped after interim analyses determined futility, while the oral TDF/FTC group continued to the planned trial conclusion. 16. After excluding women with acute HIV infection at enrollment and those with no follow-up visits, 52 incident HIV infections occurred in the oral TDF group, 61 in the TDF/FTC group, and 60 in the oral placebo group. Effectiveness was not significant for either oral PrEP medication group: −49% for TDF (HR: 1.49; 95% CI: 0.97-2.29) and −4.4% for TDF/FTC (HR: 1.04; 95% CI: 0.73-1.49). 17. However, among a subset of participants with quarterly plasma samples, tenofovir was detected in only 30% of samples from women assigned to TDF and 29% of samples from women assigned to TDF/FTC. No drug was detected at any quarterly visit for 58% of women in the TDF group and 50% in the TDF/FTC group. 18. The percentage of samples with detectable drug levels was less than 40% in all study drug groups and declined throughout the study. Multivariate analysis adjusting for baseline confounding variables found no association between drug detection and reduced risk of HIV acquisition. 19. Confirmed creatinine elevations were higher in the oral TDF/FTC group than in the oral placebo group, but no significant differences were observed between active product and placebo groups for other safety outcomes. 20. Among women determined after enrollment to have had acute HIV infection at baseline, two women in the TDF/FTC group had virus with the M184I/V mutation associated with FTC resistance. One woman in the TDF/FTC group who acquired HIV after enrollment had virus with the M184I/V mutation. No participants with HIV infection had virus with mutations associated with tenofovir resistance. 21. In summary, low adherence and operational challenges precluded reliable conclusions regarding efficacy in three trials (VOICE, FEM-PrEP, and the West African trial). However, two trials (Partners PrEP and TDF2) demonstrated significant efficacy of TDF/FTC in preventing HIV infection.
